# Pinned to callisto 0.17.0 in .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml.
# Callisto checks build attestations against that exact workflow filename; do not rename it.

# `match` is a package name ("<ecosystem>/<name>"), never a directory path.
# Root package.json is `caliper-docgen-workspace` so bare `caliper-docgen` stays unambiguous.

[changesets]
dir = ".changeset"

[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true

# The CLI binaries ship as assets of the one GitHub Release for the product package.
# The npm `bin` of `npm/caliper-docgen` cannot be a product, so the product is the Cargo crate.
# `target` matches the build matrix in callisto-release.yml; `asset-name` is the exact file name.
[release]
product-package = "cargo/caliper-docgen"
forge-repository = "orin-dx/caliper"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/caliper-docgen"
target = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
asset-name = "caliper-docgen-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/caliper-docgen"
target = "x86_64-apple-darwin"
asset-name = "caliper-docgen-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/caliper-docgen"
target = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
asset-name = "caliper-docgen-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/caliper-docgen"
target = "aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu"
asset-name = "caliper-docgen-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/caliper-docgen"
target = "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"
asset-name = "caliper-docgen-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.tar.gz"

[[package]]
match = "cargo/caliper-docgen-core"
publish-to = ["crates-io"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

[[package]]
match = "cargo/caliper-docgen-tsc-client"
publish-to = ["crates-io"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

[[package]]
match = "cargo/caliper-docgen-semantic"
publish-to = ["crates-io"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# The CLI is the product: each version gets one GitHub Release, with the
# `## <version>` section of crates/cli/CHANGELOG.md as its notes.
[[package]]
match = "cargo/caliper-docgen"
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

[[package]]
match = "npm/caliper-docgen"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# FFI shim: versioned with its npm wrapper, never published to crates.io.
[[package]]
match = "cargo/caliper-docgen-napi"
publish-to = []
release-trigger = "changeset"

[[package]]
match = "npm/caliper-docgen-napi"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

[[package]]
match = "npm/caliper-docgen-vite-plugin"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

[[package]]
match = "npm/caliper-docgen-storybook"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# The npm wrapper is meaningless without a matching binding build. The Vite plugin and the
# Storybook addon depend on the binding at an exact version (`workspace:*` publishes as an
# exact pin), so a binding release must republish them or their users never receive it.
[[fixed-group]]
name = "napi-and-binding"
members = [
  "cargo/caliper-docgen-napi",
  "npm/caliper-docgen-napi",
  "npm/caliper-docgen-vite-plugin",
  "npm/caliper-docgen-storybook",
]

# The npm wrapper redistributes this crate's binaries.
[[fixed-group]]
name = "cli-and-npm-wrapper"
members = ["cargo/caliper-docgen", "npm/caliper-docgen"]
# caliper-docgen

Faster than react-docgen-typescript; measured numbers are in `docs/performance.md`. OXC parses TypeScript/TSX; we extract React component props and emit RDT-compatible JSON via `--format rdt`. See `docs/STATUS.md` for current state and known gaps.

## Commands

```bash
cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core          # unit + snapshot tests
cargo clippy -p caliper-docgen-core -- -D warnings
cargo build --release                         # full build including CLI
```

Or use `/check` and `/snapshot` for the common workflows.

## Non-negotiables

1. No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?`
2. `FxHashMap` for internal maps; `BTreeMap` for JSON-output maps
3. `CompactString` for type/prop names in hot paths
4. No AST refs escape `parse_file()` — allocator is local per call
5. No terminal/display code in `crates/core`
6. Always emit `Diagnostic` when degrading — never fail silently

## Architecture

```
OXC parse → SourceData (extractor/) → GlobalSourceData (pipeline/) → ComponentEntry (resolver/) → ExtractionOutput
```

No reverse dependencies. `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for consumer-facing API (`pipeline/`, `types/`, `react_types`).

See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full pipeline/crate-graph overview, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (pipeline orchestration, extractor, resolver, types, serialization, CLI, NAPI binding) — start at `docs/architecture/README.md`.

## Decisions

Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing the parser choice, `PropType` serialization, the DTS cache format, panic containment or the semantic backend. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR.

## Testing discipline

Two habits that repeatedly caught real bugs during the 2026-08-12 spec-validation pass (a stale-by-one-edit watch mode, always-zero watch stats — both had zero test coverage despite extensive existing suites):

1. **Sibling-path parity.** When a function parallels an already-tested one (e.g. `WatchSession::update_file` mirrors `extract()`'s resolve/panic-containment logic; `create_session`'s guard boundary mirrors `initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s), the new path needs a test asserting the _same_ contract, not just "it runs without error." A sibling path is exactly where coverage silently lapses.
2. **Assert content, not presence.** Prefer `assert_eq!` against an exact expected value over `contains(...)`/`is_some()`/liveness checks wherever the cost is comparable. A test asserting "component X exists" survives X's props resolving to stale or wrong data; a test asserting X's exact prop set does not.

## Crate guide

- `crates/core` — pure extraction logic; @crates/core/AGENTS.md
- `crates/cli` — clap CLI, no logic; @crates/cli/AGENTS.md
- `crates/binding` — thin NAPI wrapper, delegates to core

# caliper-docgen

Faster than react-docgen-typescript; measured numbers are in `docs/performance.md`. OXC parses TypeScript/TSX; we extract React component props and emit RDT-compatible JSON via `--format rdt`. See `docs/STATUS.md` for current state and known gaps.

## Commands

```bash
cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core          # unit + snapshot tests
cargo clippy -p caliper-docgen-core -- -D warnings
cargo build --release                         # full build including CLI
```

Or use `/check` and `/snapshot` for the common workflows.

## Non-negotiables

1. No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?`
2. `FxHashMap` for internal maps; `BTreeMap` for JSON-output maps
3. `CompactString` for type/prop names in hot paths
4. No AST refs escape `parse_file()` — allocator is local per call
5. No terminal/display code in `crates/core`
6. Always emit `Diagnostic` when degrading — never fail silently

## Architecture

```
OXC parse → SourceData (extractor/) → GlobalSourceData (pipeline/) → ComponentEntry (resolver/) → ExtractionOutput
```

No reverse dependencies. `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for consumer-facing API (`pipeline/`, `types/`, `react_types`).

See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full pipeline/crate-graph overview, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (pipeline orchestration, extractor, resolver, types, serialization, CLI, NAPI binding) — start at `docs/architecture/README.md`.

## Decisions

Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing the parser choice, `PropType` serialization, the DTS cache format, panic containment or the semantic backend. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR.

## Testing discipline

Two habits that repeatedly caught real bugs during the 2026-08-12 spec-validation pass (a stale-by-one-edit watch mode, always-zero watch stats — both had zero test coverage despite extensive existing suites):

1. **Sibling-path parity.** When a function parallels an already-tested one (e.g. `WatchSession::update_file` mirrors `extract()`'s resolve/panic-containment logic; `create_session`'s guard boundary mirrors `initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s), the new path needs a test asserting the _same_ contract, not just "it runs without error." A sibling path is exactly where coverage silently lapses.
2. **Assert content, not presence.** Prefer `assert_eq!` against an exact expected value over `contains(...)`/`is_some()`/liveness checks wherever the cost is comparable. A test asserting "component X exists" survives X's props resolving to stale or wrong data; a test asserting X's exact prop set does not.

## Crate guide

- `crates/core` — pure extraction logic; @crates/core/AGENTS.md
- `crates/cli` — clap CLI, no logic; @crates/cli/AGENTS.md
- `crates/binding` — thin NAPI wrapper, delegates to core

# Releasing

How a change becomes a published release, and what to check afterwards. Callisto 0.17.0 drives it (`callisto.toml`, `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`); its own guide is `docs/releasing.md` in `orin-dx/callisto`.

## Flow

1. A pull request adds a changeset (`.changeset/`, see `AGENTS.md`).
2. On every push to `main`, the `version-pr` job opens or refreshes the release pull request `callisto/version-packages`.
3. Merging that pull request is the approval. The jobs then run in this order:

| Job | What it does | Credentials |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plan` | Derives the release from the merged commit; records whether it has CLI assets | none |
| `build` | Builds the napi addons and CLI binary for each of five targets; archives, attests and uploads the CLI asset | `id-token`, `attestations: write` |
| `assemble` | Writes the artifact manifest that binds the assets to the plan | none |
| `execute` | Publishes crates and npm packages, tags, uploads the assets and publishes the GitHub Release; verifies every attestation first | registry tokens |
| `drain` | Starts the next unfinished release, if any, once `execute` succeeds | `actions: write` |

`execute` is the only job with registry credentials. `assemble` is skipped when the plan declares no assets (`has_artifacts` is false).

The workflow runs on every push to `main`, daily at 05:23 UTC, and on manual dispatch. Every run first asks `callisto release pending` for the oldest merged release commit whose tags or GitHub Release are missing, and finishes that one before anything newer. When none is unfinished, a push to a release commit releases it and any other run refreshes the release pull request.

The workflow file must stay named `callisto-release.yml`. Callisto verifies each asset's attestation against that exact workflow path (`gh attestation verify --signer-workflow <repo>/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`), and the path is fixed in Callisto 0.17.0.

## What a release produces

| Output | Where | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Crates | crates.io | `caliper-docgen-core`, `-tsc-client`, `-semantic`, `caliper-docgen` |
| npm packages | npm, with provenance | CLI wrapper and its five platform packages, napi binding and its platform packages, Vite plugin, Storybook addon |
| Tags | this repository | One per package, such as `cargo/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` and `npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` |
| GitHub Release | this repository | One per version, on the tag `cargo/caliper-docgen@x.y.z`; notes are the `## x.y.z` section of `crates/cli/CHANGELOG.md` |
| CLI binaries | the GitHub Release | `caliper-docgen-<target>.tar.gz` for `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`; each holds the binary at the archive root |

Tag names do not change. The Homebrew tap reads the `npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` tag (`CONTRIBUTING.md`, Releases).

The build matrix in `callisto-release.yml` and the `[[release.artifact]]` entries in `callisto.toml` list the same five targets and asset names. Change both together.

## Check a release

A green run is not proof of publication. After each release:

1. Open the run's `release-receipt-attempt-N` artifact, or the receipt in the job summary, and confirm every operation succeeded.
2. `gh release view cargo/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` shows the published Release, its notes and five assets.
3. `gh attestation verify <asset> --repo orin-dx/caliper --signer-workflow orin-dx/caliper/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` passes for a downloaded asset.
4. `cargo info caliper-docgen` and `npm view caliper-docgen version` show the new version.

## Recover a failed release

A release that stopped is picked up by the next push to `main` or the daily run, and `drain` chains any further unfinished ones. While one is unfinished, the release pull request is not refreshed, and a newer release pull request published first would release without any warning that the older version was never tagged. Finish the older release first.

List what is unfinished, oldest first, with what is missing:

```sh
callisto release pending --from 2daef9276b234fcc04d8994d91210eeccd88d7e8
```

`--from` is the `RELEASE_PENDING_FROM` value in `callisto-release.yml`. Without it, `release pending` reads the committed decision of the 10 newest release commits and stops with E166 on one whose decision no longer decodes. The pin is the 0.9.0 release commit (`2daef927`).

0.9.0 was published before GitHub Releases were enabled, so `release pending` lists it as missing its GitHub Release. The first run after this flow lands finishes it: the build matrix rebuilds 0.9.0 from its release commit and Callisto creates the GitHub Release with five attested assets. Callisto adopts the crates, npm packages and tags that already landed (`docs/releasing.md` in `orin-dx/callisto`, "Publication checks"); this path has not been run, so watch that run.

- **A job failed:** "Re-run failed jobs". Callisto adopts the effects that already landed and does the rest.
- **A release cannot finish:** dispatch it by hand with its release commit, `gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha=<merged release commit>`. If it will never finish, skip it by moving `RELEASE_PENDING_FROM` to a newer release commit.

# Releasing

How a change becomes a published release, and what to check afterwards. Callisto 0.17.0 drives it (`callisto.toml`, `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`); its own guide is `docs/releasing.md` in `orin-dx/callisto`.

## Flow

1. A pull request adds a changeset (`.changeset/`, see `AGENTS.md`).
2. On every push to `main`, the `version-pr` job opens or refreshes the release pull request `callisto/version-packages`.
3. Merging that pull request is the approval. The jobs then run in this order:

| Job | What it does | Credentials |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plan` | Derives the release from the merged commit; records whether it has CLI assets | none |
| `build` | Builds the napi addons and CLI binary for each of five targets; archives, attests and uploads the CLI asset | `id-token`, `attestations: write` |
| `assemble` | Writes the artifact manifest that binds the assets to the plan | none |
| `execute` | Publishes crates and npm packages, tags, uploads the assets and publishes the GitHub Release; verifies every attestation first | registry tokens |
| `drain` | Starts the next unfinished release, if any, once `execute` succeeds | `actions: write` |

`execute` is the only job with registry credentials. `assemble` is skipped when the plan declares no assets (`has_artifacts` is false).

The workflow runs on every push to `main`, daily at 05:23 UTC, and on manual dispatch. Every run first asks `callisto release pending` for the oldest merged release commit whose tags or GitHub Release are missing, and finishes that one before anything newer. When none is unfinished, a push to a release commit releases it and any other run refreshes the release pull request.

The workflow file must stay named `callisto-release.yml`. Callisto verifies each asset's attestation against that exact workflow path (`gh attestation verify --signer-workflow <repo>/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`), and the path is fixed in Callisto 0.17.0.

## What a release produces

| Output | Where | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Crates | crates.io | `caliper-docgen-core`, `-tsc-client`, `-semantic`, `caliper-docgen` |
| npm packages | npm, with provenance | CLI wrapper and its five platform packages, napi binding and its platform packages, Vite plugin, Storybook addon |
| Tags | this repository | One per package, such as `cargo/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` and `npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` |
| GitHub Release | this repository | One per version, on the tag `cargo/caliper-docgen@x.y.z`; notes are the `## x.y.z` section of `crates/cli/CHANGELOG.md` |
| CLI binaries | the GitHub Release | `caliper-docgen-<target>.tar.gz` for `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`; each holds the binary at the archive root |

Tag names do not change. The Homebrew tap reads the `npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` tag (`CONTRIBUTING.md`, Releases).

The build matrix in `callisto-release.yml` and the `[[release.artifact]]` entries in `callisto.toml` list the same five targets and asset names. Change both together.

## Check a release

A green run is not proof of publication. After each release:

1. Open the run's `release-receipt-attempt-N` artifact, or the receipt in the job summary, and confirm every operation succeeded.
2. `gh release view cargo/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` shows the published Release, its notes and five assets.
3. `gh attestation verify <asset> --repo orin-dx/caliper --signer-workflow orin-dx/caliper/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` passes for a downloaded asset.
4. `cargo info caliper-docgen` and `npm view caliper-docgen version` show the new version.

## Recover a failed release

A release that stopped is picked up by the next push to `main` or the daily run, and `drain` chains any further unfinished ones. While one is unfinished, the release pull request is not refreshed, and a newer release pull request published first would release without any warning that the older version was never tagged. Finish the older release first.

List what is unfinished, oldest first, with what is missing:

```sh
callisto release pending --from 2daef9276b234fcc04d8994d91210eeccd88d7e8
```

`--from` is the `RELEASE_PENDING_FROM` value in `callisto-release.yml`. Without it, `release pending` reads the committed decision of the 10 newest release commits and stops with E166 on one whose decision no longer decodes. The pin is the 0.9.0 release commit (`2daef927`).

0.9.0 was published before GitHub Releases were enabled, so `release pending` lists it as missing its GitHub Release. The first run after this flow lands finishes it: the build matrix rebuilds 0.9.0 from its release commit and Callisto creates the GitHub Release with five attested assets. Callisto adopts the crates, npm packages and tags that already landed (`docs/releasing.md` in `orin-dx/callisto`, "Publication checks"); this path has not been run, so watch that run.

- **E148, release PR snapshot changed:** the `version-pr` job planned from a release PR that changed before it applied the plan. Nothing was changed. Re-run the failed job, or push to `main` again.
- **`ArtifactAssetDiffers`:** a rebuilt asset is not byte-identical to the one already on the draft Release. Delete the mismatched asset, then dispatch the workflow again with the release commit:

  ```sh

  gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha=<merged release commit>
  ```

- **E140, attestation verification failed:** `gh attestation verify` rejected an asset: wrong repository, signer workflow, signer digest, source digest, or a self-hosted runner. The signer digest is the commit that ran `plan` (`--orchestration-revision`), so recover by re-running the whole workflow so `plan`, `build` and `execute` share one revision.

CI checks this weekly ([`docs/performance.md`](docs/performance.md)). Whether the types are right is judged against TypeScript's checker, not against `react-docgen-typescript`: on the props both tools list, the checker contradicts Caliper on 0 to 1.09% and `react-docgen-typescript` on 0.006 to 5.02%, depending on the corpus (weekly run of 2026-11-06, [`docs/rdt-differences.md`](docs/rdt-differences.md)). content.content:
The structural result returns immediately. The semantic result follows: the CLI waits for it behind an opt-in flag, and the NAPI binding exposes a second async call so the Vite plugin can patch when it resolves. Spawn `tsc` at the start of the run so it loads while extraction runs. Each result carries a content hash, and a stale one is dropped.

## Slice 1 (experimental, off by default)

`caliper-docgen extract --experimental-semantic-types [--tsc-path PATH]`, or `experimentalSemanticTypes` and `tscPath` in `docgen.config.ts`. `crates/semantic` spawns the project's `node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --api` or `node_modules/tsrs/bin/tsrs --api` (see "Supported binaries"), builds one program over the files of the components the structural pass found, and asks for each exported function component its call signature's first parameter and that type's properties. The CLI then calls core's `merge_semantic`. Not wired into watch, `check`, `inspect` or the NAPI binding.

- **Merge:** props present, `type`, `required`, `parent`, `declarations` and the component's `composes` from the checker, and its description and tags where it has them (see "Declarations, tags and composes"); `defaultValue`, inheritance layers, curated inherited props and `discriminantProp` stay structural. The checker is asked for a prop's description only when the structural pass has none (65% of Mantine's requests otherwise). Props `@types/react` declares are excluded by declaring file. Identical merged props are shared, as in the structural result.
- **Output type:** no new `PropType` variant and no schema change. Primitives, literals, unions (with `boolean` collapsed and `undefined` dropped from optional props), arrays, tuples, inline objects of up to 16 fields and single-signature functions map onto existing variants; `ReactNode`, `ElementType`, `CSSProperties` and `ReactElement` map to their terminals; anything else (named interfaces, enums, generics, overloads, anything past depth 4) is `Named` with the checker's own text. Union members keep the checker's order, which is creation order, not source order.
- **Names:** a symbol's `name` from the checker is its escaped name: a name that starts with two underscores has a third (`__size` arrives as `___size`, TypeScript's `escapeLeadingUnderscores`, so that it cannot collide with internal names such as `__call`). `rpc.rs` removes it when the answer is read, so every name downstream is the one the source writes.
- **Error type:** a name the checker cannot resolve (an import that does not resolve, a name declared nowhere) is typed with its error type, which carries the flags of `any`. Only `Type.intrinsicName` tells it from a written `any`: `"error"` against `"any"`, and the error type has an id per site, so the `any` id says nothing. `rpc.rs` reads `intrinsicName`; `convert.rs` turns an `"error"` type into an `opaque` type with the reason `unresolvableImport` (its `specifier` is the name as the source writes it, since the checker does not say which module was behind it), so the prop has `degradedBy: ["unresolvableImport"]` and a written `any` stays `any` with none. No new diagnostic code.
- **Provenance:** `Info` diagnostics with code `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` whose `affects` lists the output keys: one for the components the checker resolved, one per fallback reason. A first-class per-component field would change the canonical JSON and needs a `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump (`crates/core/src/types/output.rs`).
- **Fallback:** a missing, unsupported-version, crashed or timed-out `tsc` gives the structural result plus one `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning, never an error. Per component, the structural result stands for: not exported, class or non-function, overloaded, no props parameter, `any`/`unknown`/union props type, a generic component whose instantiation at its default could not be formed (see "Generic components"), none of the exports the extractor recorded for it found (or found declared in another file), a generic sub-component reached through its parent's property, or a request the checker rejected. Each is listed with its reason.
- **Which export:** the extractor records how the module exports each component (ADR 0027): its export names (`default` included), or for a sub-component attached to an exported one the path through that export (`Menu.Item = Item` beside `export default Menu` is `default.Item`). The checker asks for exactly those, follows an alias to what it aliases, reads an attached sub-component as the property of its parent's type, and checks that the declaration is in the component's file. It never takes the module's `default` unless `default` is a recorded export, and never looks a component up by its display name. Each request carries the component's output key, its answer or fallback carries it back, and the merge (whole-project and session, in time or late) finds the entry by that key alone.
- **Parameter markers:** the checker's parameter symbols carry no optional or rest flag (an optional parameter has the same flags and `checkFlags` as a required one), so `convert.rs` reads them from what the checker prints for the function type: `name?: T` is optional and its `undefined` is dropped from the type, as for an optional prop, `...name: T[]` is the rest parameter; the signature's `flags` (`HasRestParameter`, bit 1) say the last parameter is a rest parameter either way. A parameter whose type is written `T | undefined` stays required. The type is printed with `typeToString` flags `NoTruncation | InTypeAlias` (plus the checker's own defaults): an alias at the top (`type Handler = (value?: string) => void`) is printed as the parameter list it stands for, not as `Handler`, and nothing is cut short. A `this` parameter is printed but is not one of the signature's parameters, and an overload set or a function with properties is printed as an object type whose signatures are read in order. When the printed type still does not give one entry per parameter (a callable interface prints as its name whatever the flags), a parameter is never taken to be required: the type is `opaque` with reason `unsupportedExpression`, so the prop carries `degradedBy`.
- **Not carried:** index signatures, `readonly` and ref names (`PropType` has them since `SCHEMA_VERSION` 4; `convert.rs` doesn't set them), generic parameters of functions.
- **Tests:** `crates/semantic/tests/replay.rs` runs the backend against `replay-tsc`, which answers from a recording of the real `7.1.0-beta` (`tests/fixtures/recording.json`, refreshed by `cargo run -p caliper-docgen-semantic --example record_fixture -- <typescript package dir>`; the `markers` fixture project, for names and parameters, records to `tests/fixtures/markers.recording.json` with the fixture name as a second argument; the `errors` fixture records the error type); a request the recording lacks fails the test. Fallbacks (no `tsc`, unsupported version, bad path, crash, hang) are asserted as the structural output plus one warning. The CLI test asserts the default output has no `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic.

Measured on `7.1.0-beta`, `extract --json` (best of 2 to 3), flag on against off, plus the base commit's output compared byte for byte (identical apart from `durationMs` on all five corpora, with and without `--load-dependencies`). Peak RSS is the larger of the two processes; on Chakra Caliper is 117 MiB and `tsc` 945 MiB.

| Corpus   | Components resolved by the checker |            Off |              On |
| -------- | ---------------------------------: | -------------: | --------------: |
| mantine  |                          332 / 344 |  47 ms, 82 MiB | 588 ms, 287 MiB |
| chakra   |                          598 / 598 |  38 ms, 68 MiB |  9.3 s, 975 MiB |
| shadcn   |                      1,693 / 1,884 |  48 ms, 81 MiB |  1.5 s, 874 MiB |
| antd     |                          206 / 248 |  36 ms, 69 MiB | 508 ms, 443 MiB |
| spectrum |                      1,153 / 1,356 | 71 ms, 118 MiB | 618 ms, 381 MiB |

Chakra's time is `tsc` computing 470,000 shared props' types, not round trips. Before shared props were interned in the merge, Caliper itself held 7.4 GiB on Chakra.

Against the oracle (`scripts/weekly.py --oracle`, flag on, `7.1.0-beta`), wrong verdicts fall to 0.0% on every corpus but antd (0.1%), but the identical-or-spelled share also falls: mantine 91.3% to 22.0%, chakra 100% to 16.4%, shadcn 85.2% to 52.3%, antd 91.9% to 82.3%, spectrum 83.2% to 28.3%. The oracle credits the structural result for keeping a type's name (`StyleProp<MantineSpacing>`); the checker's answer is expanded to its members and compared as "less precise". Keeping the alias name and arguments needs a `PropType` that carries them, which is an output change.

### Supported binaries

Two packages provide the `--api` server, and both are used through the same client; neither is the default checker (the flag stays opt-in).

- **`typescript`** from 7.1 on (`7.1.0-beta`, rc and stable): `node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc`.
- **`tsrs`** (`oxc-project/tsrs`, a Rust port of the TypeScript 7 checker): `node_modules/tsrs/bin/tsrs`, a Node shim that starts the platform binary from `@tsrs/<platform>`. Traced on the wire against `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`: the same method sequence and the same results as `typescript@7.1.0-beta` on three recordings, and identical canonical output on Chakra, rdt-compat and blueprint.

**Discovery.** `--tsc-path` (or `tscPath`) wins and must exist. Otherwise the search walks up from the project root and takes the first `node_modules` that holds either binary; inside one `node_modules`, `typescript/bin/tsc` comes before `tsrs/bin/tsrs`, so an install that has both keeps using `typescript`. Pass `--tsc-path` to choose `tsrs` there. The platform binary (`node_modules/@tsrs/<platform>/tsrs`) can be given with `--tsc-path` too and starts without Node.

**Version rule** (`crates/tsc-client/src/supervisor.rs`, list in `crates/semantic/src/lib.rs`, `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS`). The version is read from the `package.json` of the package that owns the binary: the parent of `bin` for `typescript/bin/tsc` and `tsrs/bin/tsrs`, the binary's own directory for `@tsrs/<platform>/tsrs`. An entry is an exact version or a `major.minor` series. A `tsrs` version reads `<tsrs version>-ts<typescript version>`; it is accepted only when it is listed exactly (today `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the build that was traced) and its TypeScript part is also taken by a TypeScript entry (`7.1`). A new `tsrs` release is therefore refused until someone traces it and adds it, as for any other build.

The protocol detail that matters for `tsrs` is unchanged from `typescript`: the client sends `createPrograms[].compilerOptions` (the Node client sends `options`; the server accepts both, and `crates/semantic/tests/replay.rs` pins the key). Set `TSRS_BIN` to a `tsrs` binary to run `crates/semantic/tests/tsrs_real.rs` against the real thing; without it the test returns at once.

## On demand, per component (experimental, off by default)

Caliper is pre-v1. [`docs/STATUS.md`](docs/STATUS.md) lists what works, and [`docs/edge-cases.md`](docs/edge-cases.md) the known gaps. Conditional types and mapped types over an unbound generic need a real type checker, which OXC deliberately isn't.

## Install

```bash
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen                # CLI, with the prebuilt binary for your platform
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-vite-plugin    # Vite plugin
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-storybook      # Storybook 11 addon
cargo install caliper-docgen                         # CLI from crates.io
```

Coming from `react-docgen-typescript`? [`MIGRATING.md`](MIGRATING.md) covers what's compatible today.

## Quick start

Per component, the structural result stands for: not exported, class or non-function, overloaded, no props parameter, `any`/`unknown`/union props type, a generic component whose instantiation at its default could not be formed (see "Generic components"), none of the exports the extractor recorded for it found (or found declared in another file), a generic sub-component reached through its parent's property, or a request the checker rejected. Each is listed with its reason.
- **Which export:** the extractor records how the module exports each component (ADR 0027): its export names (`default` included), or for a sub-component attached to an exported one the path through that export (`Menu.Item = Item` beside `export default Menu` is `default.Item`). The checker asks for exactly those, follows an alias to what it aliases, reads an attached sub-component as the property of its parent's type, and checks that the declaration is in the component's file. It never takes the module's `default` unless `default` is a recorded export, and never looks a component up by its display name. Each request carries the component's output key, its answer or fallback carries it back, and the merge (whole-project and session, in time or late) finds the entry by that key alone.
- **Parameter markers:** the checker's parameter symbols carry no optional or rest flag (an optional parameter has the same flags and `checkFlags` as a required one), so `convert.rs` reads them from what the checker prints for the function type: `name?: T` is optional and its `undefined` is dropped from the type, as for an optional prop, `...name: T[]` is the rest parameter; the signature's `flags` (`HasRestParameter`, bit 1) say the last parameter is a rest parameter either way. A parameter whose type is written `T | undefined` stays required. The type is printed with `typeToString` flags `NoTruncation | InTypeAlias` (plus the checker's own defaults): an alias at the top (`type Handler = (value?: string) => void`) is printed as the parameter list it stands for, not as `Handler`, and nothing is cut short. A `this` parameter is printed but is not one of the signature's parameters, and an overload set or a function with properties is printed as an object type whose signatures are read in order. When the printed type still does not give one entry per parameter (a callable interface prints as its name whatever the flags), a parameter is never taken to be required: the type is `opaque` with reason `unsupportedExpression`, so the prop carries `degradedBy`.
- **Not carried:** index signatures, `readonly` and ref names (`PropType` has them since `SCHEMA_VERSION` 4; `convert.rs` doesn't set them), generic parameters of functions.
- **Tests:** `crates/semantic/tests/replay.rs` runs the backend against `replay-tsc`, which answers from a recording of the real `7.1.0-beta` (`tests/fixtures/recording.json`, refreshed by `cargo run -p caliper-docgen-semantic --example record_fixture -- <typescript package dir>`; the `markers` fixture project, for names and parameters, records to `tests/fixtures/markers.recording.json` with the fixture name as a second argument; the `errors` fixture records the error type); a request the recording lacks fails the test. Fallbacks (no `tsc`, unsupported version, bad path, crash, hang) are asserted as the structural output plus one warning. The CLI test asserts the default output has no `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic.

Measured on `7.1.0-beta`, `extract --json` (best of 2 to 3), flag on against off, plus the base commit's output compared byte for byte (identical apart from `durationMs` on all five corpora, with and without `--load-dependencies`). Peak RSS is the larger of the two processes; on Chakra Caliper is 117 MiB and `tsc` 945 MiB.

| Corpus   | Components resolved by the checker |            Off |              On |
| -------- | ---------------------------------: | -------------: | --------------: |
| mantine  |                          332 / 344 |  47 ms, 82 MiB | 588 ms, 287 MiB |
| chakra   |                          598 / 598 |  38 ms, 68 MiB |  9.3 s, 975 MiB |
| shadcn   |                      1,693 / 1,884 |  48 ms, 81 MiB |  1.5 s, 874 MiB |
| antd     |                          206 / 248 |  36 ms, 69 MiB | 508 ms, 443 MiB |
| spectrum |                      1,153 / 1,356 | 71 ms, 118 MiB | 618 ms, 381 MiB |

Chakra's time is `tsc` computing 470,000 shared props' types, not round trips. Before shared props were interned in the merge, Caliper itself held 7.4 GiB on Chakra.

Against the oracle (`scripts/weekly.py --oracle`, flag on, `7.1.0-beta`), wrong verdicts fall to 0.0% on every corpus but antd (0.1%), but the identical-or-spelled share also falls: mantine 91.3% to 22.0%, chakra 100% to 16.4%, shadcn 85.2% to 52.3%, antd 91.9% to 82.3%, spectrum 83.2% to 28.3%. The oracle credits the structural result for keeping a type's name (`StyleProp<MantineSpacing>`); the checker's answer is expanded to its members and compared as "less precise". Keeping the alias name and arguments needs a `PropType` that carries them, which is an output change.

### Supported binaries

Two packages provide the `--api` server, and both are used through the same client; neither is the default checker (the flag stays opt-in).

- **`typescript`** from 7.1 on (`7.1.0-beta`, rc and stable): `node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc`.
- **`tsrs`** (`oxc-project/tsrs`, a Rust port of the TypeScript 7 checker): `node_modules/tsrs/bin/tsrs`, a Node shim that starts the platform binary from `@tsrs/<platform>`. Traced on the wire against `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`: the same method sequence and the same results as `typescript@7.1.0-beta` on three recordings, and identical canonical output on Chakra, rdt-compat and blueprint.

**Discovery.** `--tsc-path` (or `tscPath`) wins and must exist. Otherwise the search walks up from the project root and takes the first `node_modules` that holds either binary; inside one `node_modules`, `typescript/bin/tsc` comes before `tsrs/bin/tsrs`, so an install that has both keeps using `typescript`. Pass `--tsc-path` to choose `tsrs` there. The platform binary (`node_modules/@tsrs/<platform>/tsrs`) can be given with `--tsc-path` too and starts without Node.

**Version rule** (`crates/tsc-client/src/supervisor.rs`, list in `crates/semantic/src/lib.rs`, `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS`). The version is read from the `package.json` of the package that owns the binary: the parent of `bin` for `typescript/bin/tsc` and `tsrs/bin/tsrs`, the binary's own directory for `@tsrs/<platform>/tsrs`. An entry is an exact version or a `major.minor` series. A `tsrs` version reads `<tsrs version>-ts<typescript version>`; it is accepted only when it is listed exactly (today `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the build that was traced) and its TypeScript part is also taken by a TypeScript entry (`7.1`). A new `tsrs` release is therefore refused until someone traces it and adds it, as for any other build.

The protocol detail that matters for `tsrs` is unchanged from `typescript`: the client sends `createPrograms[].compilerOptions` (the Node client sends `options`; the server accepts both, and `crates/semantic/tests/replay.rs` pins the key). Set `TSRS_BIN` to a `tsrs` binary to run `crates/semantic/tests/tsrs_real.rs` against the real thing; without it the test returns at once.

## On demand, per component (experimental, off by default)

Caliper is pre-v1. [`docs/STATUS.md`](docs/STATUS.md) lists what works, and [`docs/edge-cases.md`](docs/edge-cases.md) the known gaps. Conditional types and mapped types over an unbound generic need a real type checker, which OXC deliberately isn't.

## Install

```bash
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen                # CLI, with the prebuilt binary for your platform
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-vite-plugin    # Vite plugin
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-storybook      # Storybook 11 addon
cargo install caliper-docgen                         # CLI from crates.io
```

Coming from `react-docgen-typescript`? [`MIGRATING.md`](MIGRATING.md) covers what's compatible today.
